description:
Worth defending: the AlertTrigger enum in jmap-jscalendar-types (re-exported here at lib.rs:64-68) carries an Unknown(serde_json::Value) catch-all variant in addition to OffsetTrigger and AbsoluteTrigger.

RFC 8984 §4.5.2 normatively says: 'Implementations MUST NOT trigger for trigger types they do not understand but MUST preserve them.' The Unknown variant is exactly what makes that preservation possible — without it, a deserialize of an unknown @type would either fail or silently drop, both of which violate the spec MUST.

A future contributor doing an 'enum hygiene' pass might:
  - Remove the Unknown variant ('exhaustive enums are cleaner').
  - Replace it with #[serde(other)] ('idiomatic Rust').
  - Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to the enum.

All three would break round-trip preservation. The verifying test is alert_unknown_trigger_roundtrip (tests/types_test.rs:798-820).

Cross-reference: workspace AGENTS.md 'Extras-preservation policy' for the forward-compat catch-all pattern. AlertTrigger is the type-tagged-enum case of the same policy applied to data-shape unions instead of string enums.
title: decision: AlertTrigger::Unknown(Value) for forward-compat per RFC 8984 §4.5.2
